# iliad-106 — renderings chosen for 16.676–776 (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ ἐπικερτομέων προσέφης Πατρόκλεες ἱππεῦ (16.744, whole-line speech introduction; second person) | "Him, taunting, you addressed, Patroclus the horseman:" | "Taunting him, you said to him, Patroclus the horseman:" | "mocking", "jeering"; follows the table's 16.20 row (προσέφης Πατρόκλεες ἱππεῦ) and the Odyssey's ἐπικερτομέων (22.194) |
| Διὸς κρείσσων νόος ἠέ περ ἀνδρῶν (16.688) | "of Zeus stronger is the mind than that of men indeed" | "the mind of Zeus is always stronger than that of men" | "greater", "mightier" (kept for φέρτερος); κρείσσων "stronger" as in iliad-001 (1.80) |
| ὅς τε καὶ ἄλκιμον ἄνδρα φοβεῖ καὶ ἀφείλετο νίκην (16.689) | "puts to flight … takes away victory" | "puts even the valiant man to flight and easily takes his victory away" | "terrifies", "scares"; φοβέω "put to flight"; the aorist ἀφείλετο is a general truth, so present in English |
| θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ἀνῆκεν (16.691) | "the spirit in his chest urged on" | "urged on the spirit in his chest" | "let loose", "unleashed" (decide the sense); follows the published iliad-038 and -041 (6.256, 7.24), where ἀνίημι with θυμός is "urged" |
| μετεκίαθε (16.685, with the accusative) | "went after" | "went after" | "pursued", "followed"; μετακιαθέω "go after" (the glossary has "go through" for 11.714, a different use) |
| ἐκ βελέων (16.678) · βέλος of a thrown stone (16.737, οὐδ’ ἁλίωσε βέλος) | "out of the missiles" · "he make the missile vain" | "out of the missiles" · "the missile fail" | "shafts" — the older Iliad rows (1.382, 4.185, 5.18) fix βέλος as "shaft", but 16.668 (iliad-105) already ships ἐκ βελέων as "missiles", the two lines answer each other, and a stone is not a shaft; the older rows are for arrows and spears. The clash between the old "shaft" rows and the 16.668 row needs deciding when the table is next touched |
| ἐϋδμήτου ἐπὶ πύργου (16.700) | "upon the well-built tower" | "on the well-built tower" | "well-constructed" (the Odyssey's ἐϋδμήτους, odyssey-030, -106); follows the Iliad's iliad-073 "well-built towers" |
| ὀλοὰ φρονέων (16.701) | "baneful things thinking" | "with baneful thoughts" | "deadly intent", "plotting ruin"; ὀλοός "baneful" (3.133, 1.342) |
| ἔστη τῷ … (16.701) | "had stood against him" | "had taken his stand against him" | "stood by him", "stood over him" |
| ἐπ’ ἀγκῶνος … τείχεος (16.702) | "upon the elbow of the … wall" | "onto a jutting corner of the … wall" | "battlement", "parapet", "angle" (each decides the structure); ἀγκών "elbow" (10.80), the note gives the usual explanation |
| ἀπεστυφέλιξεν (16.703) | "thrust back" | "drove back" | "pushed back", "shoved back"; follows the published iliad-031 (5.437) and στυφελίζω "thrust roughly" / "shove" (7.261) |
| χείρεσσ’ ἀθανάτῃσι … νύσσων (16.704) | "with immortal hands striking" | "striking … with his immortal hands" | "stabbing" (the published rendering for νύσσω with spears, iliad-069, -078), "jabbing", "prodding" |
| χάζεο … οὔ νύ τοι αἶσα (16.707) | "Give ground … not now for you is it the portion" | "Give ground … it is not your lot" | "retreat", "fate" (reserved for μοῖρα, πότμος, μόρος); χάζομαι "give ground" (5.702, 11.539), αἶσα "portion" / "lot" (1.416) |
| δίζε γὰρ ἠὲ μάχοιτο … ἦ … ὁμοκλήσειεν ἀλῆναι (16.713–714) | "he was in two minds whether he should fight … or call … with a shout to crowd into the wall" | "he was in two minds whether to … fight again, or to call the people with a shout to crowd into the wall" | "debated", "pondered" (reserved for μερμηρίζω "be in doubt"), "rally the people"; δίζω "be in two minds"; εἰλέω (ἀλῆναι) "crowd together" |
| αἰζηῷ (adjective with ἀνέρι, of Asius, 16.716) | "vigorous" | "vigorous" | "vigorous young man" (the table's αἰζηός, which suits young men, not Hecuba's brother); the noun keeps the table's "vigorous young men" |
| μήτρως … αὐτοκασίγνητος Ἑκάβης (16.717–718) | "mother’s-brother of Hector … own brother of Hecuba" | "the mother’s brother of Hector … own brother of Hecuba" | "uncle" alone (loses the mother); follows the table's μήτρως (2.662) and αὐτοκασίγνητος (3.238) |
| Ἕκτορ τίπτε μάχης ἀποπαύεαι; (16.721) | "why from battle do you cease?" | "why are you leaving off from the battle?" | "hold back", "stop fighting" (add a verb); ἀποπαύομαι "cease from" |
| στυγερῶς … ἀπερωήσειας (16.723) | "hatefully … you would draw back" | "you would soon draw back from war, hatefully" | "to your cost", "in dismay" (each decides the force of the adverb, which is not known); ἀπερωέω "draw back"; στυγερός "hateful" (4.240) |
| ἔφεπε κρατερώνυχας ἵππους (16.724, 16.732) | "drive the strong-hoofed horses" | "drive your strong-hoofed horses at" / "drove his strong-hoofed horses at" | "pursue", "press on" (kept for the published ἔφεπε of Agamemnon, iliad-065, which has persons as object); κρατερώνυχας "strong-hoofed" (6.253) |
| ἵππους ἐς πόλεμον πεπληγέμεν (16.728) | "the horses into the war to lash" | "to lash the horses into the war" | "whip", "drive on"; πλήσσω "strike", of a charioteer's whip "lash" |
| οὐδ’ ἐνάριζεν (16.731) | "was not despoiling" | "did not strip them of their armour" | "did not kill", "slew" (the table's ἐνάριζον "killing" at 9.530 is for the context where the killing is the point); ἐναρίζω "strip" (5.155) |
| ἧκε δ’ ἐρεισάμενος (16.736) | "and sent it, bracing himself" | "and sent it, bracing himself" | "hurled", "threw" (kept for βάλλω), "let fly" (kept for ἀφίημι); ἵημι "send"; ἐρείδομαι "brace oneself" (12.457) |
| οὐδ’ ἁλίωσε βέλος (16.737) | "he make the missile vain" | "the missile fail" | "did not miss", "was not wasted"; ἁλιόω "make vain" |
| Κεβριόνην νόθον υἱὸν ἀγακλῆος Πριάμοιο (16.738) | "Cebriones, a bastard son of renowned Priam" | "Cebriones, an illegitimate son of renowned Priam" | "famous Priam" (κλυτός), "glorious" (κυδάλιμος); νόθος "bastard" / "illegitimate" (iliad-068); ἀγακλεής "renowned" (ἀγα- the intensifier of ἀγακλυτός) |
| ἀμφοτέρας δ’ ὀφρῦς σύνελεν λίθος, οὐδέ οἱ ἔσχεν ὀστέον (16.740) | "both his brows the stone crushed together, and not for him did hold the bone" | "crushed both his brows together and the bone did not hold" | "smashed", "shattered"; συναιρέω "crush together"; ἔσχεν "held (out)" |
| ὢ πόποι ἦ μάλ’ ἐλαφρὸς ἀνήρ, ὡς ῥεῖα κυβιστᾷ (16.745) | "Ah! truly very light is the man, how easily he tumbles!" | "Ah, truly, what a light man he is, and how easily he tumbles!" | "nimble" (kept for ῥίμφα), "acrobat", "dive" for κυβιστάω (the diver is ἀρνευτήρ, 16.742); ὢ πόποι "Ah" (table), ῥεῖα "easily", ἐλαφρός "light" (12.450) |
| κυβιστητῆρες (16.750) | "tumblers" | "tumblers" | "acrobats", "divers"; κυβιστητήρ is built on κυβιστάω "tumble" |
| τήθεα διφῶν (16.747) | "oysters searching for" | "searching for oysters" | "shellfish", "sea-urchins"; the usual identification, the note says so |
| ἦ ῥα καὶ ἐν Τρώεσσι κυβιστητῆρες ἔασιν (16.750) | "Truly then, among the Trojans too there are tumblers." | "Truly, there are tumblers among the Trojans, too." | "So he spoke, and" — ἦ ῥα here is not the narrative ἦ ῥα καί of the table's 8.416 row; the note says so |
| οἶμα λέοντος (16.752) | "the rush of a lion" | "the rush of a lion" | "the way of a lion", "the spirit of a lion"; οἶμα "rush" on the usual explanation, the note says it is rare |
| ὣς ἐπὶ Κεβριόνῃ Πατρόκλεες ἆλσο μεμαώς (16.754, second person) | "so upon Cebriones, Patroclus, you leapt, eager" | "so, Patroclus, you leapt upon Cebriones, eager" | "sprang", "rushed" (σεύω); ἅλλομαι "leap" (5.494), μεμαώς "eager" (7.261) |
| λέονθ’ ὣς δηρινθήτην … ἄμφω πεινάοντε μέγα φρονέοντε μάχεσθον (16.756–758, duals) | "like two lions contended … both hungry, both greatly thinking, fight" | "like two lions that fight … both hungry, both full of proud thoughts" | "wrangled", "quarrelled" (kept for ἐριδαίνω); μέγα φρονέων "greatly thinking" / "full of proud thoughts" (11.296) |
| Ἕκτωρ μὲν κεφαλῆφιν ἐπεὶ λάβεν οὐχὶ μεθίει (16.762) | "when by the head he took hold, did not let go" | "once he had taken hold of the head, did not let go" | "grasped", "gripped"; follows the published iliad-098 (15.716) "took hold … did not let go" |
| Εὖρός τε Νότος τ’ ἐριδαίνετον (16.765) | "the East Wind and the South Wind quarrel with one another" | same | "contend" (turned down for ἐριδαίνω, 1.574); the table's four-winds row |
| βήσσῃς · βαθέην … ὕλην (16.766) | "glens" · "deep forest" | "glens" · "deep forest" | "ravines", "valleys", "thickets"; βήσσα "glen"; ὕλη "forest" (2.455) |
| φηγόν · μελίην · τανύφλοιον · κράνειαν (16.767) | "oak" · "ash" · "long-barked" · "cornel" | same | "beech" (the English name of φηγός, which is an oak, as in the table's 5.838 row), "ash-spear" (the weapon, kept for μελίη in the table), "thin-barked", "dogwood" |
| τανυήκεας ὄζους (16.768) | "long-pointed boughs" | "long-pointed boughs" | "long-leaved", "slender"; τανυ- "stretched, long" (12.237); the Odyssey table’s τανυήκης (22.443, swords) is "long-edged", with a note that the second element (ἀκή "point, edge") is not certain; boughs have no edge, so "long-pointed" here is a departure, and the note says the same doubt |
| πάταγος … ἀγνυμενάων (16.769) | "a crashing of them breaking" | "a crashing of them as they break" | "clatter" (kept for ὀδόντων), "roar"; πάταγος "crashing" |
| ἐστυφέλιξαν ἀσπίδας (of rocks, 16.774) | "thrust roughly the shields" | "battered the shields" | "shoved" (the `i` for persons), "knocked", "shook"; στυφελίζω "thrust roughly" |
| στροφάλιγγι κονίης · μέγας μεγαλωστί · λελασμένος ἱπποσυνάων (16.775–776) | "in the whirl of dust … great in his greatness … forgetful of his horsemanship" | "in the whirl of dust … stretched out at full length … forgetful of his horsemanship" | the published Odyssey wording of the same line (odyssey-115, 24.39–40), with person changed; ἱπποσύνη "horsemanship" (4.303) |
| Names: Ἄδρηστος · Αὐτόνοος · Ἔχεκλος · Πέριμος Μεγάδης · Ἐπίστωρ · Μελάνιππος · Ἔλασος · Μούλιος · Πυλάρτης (16.694–696) | "Adrastus … Autonous … Echeclus … Perimus, Megas’-son … Epistor … Melanippus … Elasus … Mulius … Pylartes" | "Adrastus … Perimus, son of Megas … Mulius …" | "Adrestus", "Autonoos", "Moulios" (Greek spellings); the Latinised forms of the published parts (Adrastus, Autonous, Melanippus, Pylartes) and the table's Mulius; Μεγάδης read as a patronymic |

Note on a choice that is the drafter's, not the table's: at 16.705–706 the free English names Apollo as the speaker ("Apollo shouted dreadfully at him and spoke winged words"), because the Greek subject of the participle is left unsaid after Patroclus is the subject of ἐπέσσυτο; the note says so. The published iliad-031 (5.438–439) names him because its Greek does.
